title: Waste and recycling
audience: Commercial cleaners who manage waste streams and recycling on client sites.
learningOutcomes: Separate general waste, recycling and regulated waste streams in the labelled containers.
Reduce waste where the contract and the site allow it, without mixing streams.
Refer any unclear or regulated waste to the site for disposal under its plan.

instruction.heading: Separating the streams
instruction.body: Waste on a client site usually falls into a few streams: general waste, recycling, food waste where the site has a food waste service, and any material the site has identified as regulated or special. Keep the streams apart from the point where the waste is created. Use the labelled containers and the collection routes the site sets, and do not place a bag in a bin because it is nearest. A mixed bin usually goes to general waste, and a single item in the wrong bin can spoil a whole load of recycling. Check the label on a container before you use it, not just its colour, because a colour may mean one thing at one site and something else at another. If a container has no label, treat its contents as unknown until the site has identified them. Keep the waste areas tidy, with lids closed and bins not overfilled, so that the streams stay identifiable and no leak reaches a drain.

instruction.heading: Reducing waste within the rules
instruction.body: Reducing waste is part of good service. The EPA's guidance on the general environmental duty describes the same approach in a different setting: avoid creating waste where possible, reuse what can be reused, recycle what can be recycled, and separate and store each type safely. In a cleaning job, that means ordering consumables to need rather than in excess, reusing cloths and mop heads where the method allows, and refilling only from approved, labelled bulk containers. Do not refill a spray bottle from an unlabelled drum, because nobody can then say what is in the bottle. Do not reuse single-use items in a way the site does not permit, for example a disposable glove or a sachet that the site has said to discard after one use. Where a reduction would change the cleaning method or product, the change belongs to the contract or site procedure, not to the cleaner.

instruction.heading: Unclear and regulated waste
instruction.body: When you cannot say what a material is, do not decide its stream yourself. Leave it in place, do not put it in a bin, and record its location and the time. Refer it to the site contact so that the site can identify it and dispose of it under its plan. Victoria's general environmental duty requires a business to reduce or eliminate the risk of harm from its waste, so far as reasonably practicable. The duty applies to businesses as well as households, and the EPA states that businesses that fail to meet it face significant penalties (EPA Victoria, updated 4 August 2026). EPA Victoria's industrial waste guidance also says that anyone who manages industrial waste must classify it and meet the duties for that classification, and that managing waste includes collecting, transporting, storing and disposing of it (EPA Victoria, updated 9 April 2026). The cleaner does not classify waste. The site does, under its plan and any authorisation it holds.

instruction.heading: Leaks and spills in the waste area
instruction.body: A leaking bag or container in a waste area is both a hazard and a pathway to a drain. Stop, keep other people away, and check the label and the SDS for any chemical involved before touching it. Use the absorbent material and the gloves the site supplies. Do not wash the leak into a floor drain or a stormwater drain. The EPA's stormwater guidance says that waste should be kept out of stormwater drains so far as reasonably practicable (EPA Victoria, updated 7 May 2025). Record the leak, the time, the area and the action taken, and refer the clean-up of anything beyond the routine to the site.

procedure: Separate general waste, recycling, food waste and any identified regulated waste into the labelled containers the site provides.
Use the collection routes the site sets, and keep each stream apart from the point where it is created.
Reduce waste through reuse, avoiding excess orders and approved, labelled bulk refills only.
Leave any unclear or regulated material in place, and refer it to the site for disposal under its plan.
Record the item, its location and the time, and the person notified.
For a leak or spill, stop, keep people away, check the SDS, use the site's absorbent, and do not wash it into a drain.

workedExamples.situation: A bin marked recycling contains a sealed container with no label.
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not put the container in the recycling or the general bin. Leave it where it is, record its location and the time, and refer it to the site contact so that the site can identify and dispose of it under its plan. Do not open it or try to identify it by smell or by the colour of the liquid.

workedExamples.situation: During a bin round, a cleaner finds a cleaning product container leaking into the bottom of a waste bin in the loading area.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What are the first three actions?
workedExamples.reasoning: Stop, and keep other people away from the leak. Check the label and the SDS on the register, and use the absorbent the site has supplied with the gloves it specifies. Do not pour water on the leak or wash it toward the drain. Record the time, the location and the product name, and refer the clean-up to the site, which decides whether anything beyond the routine needs specialist help.

workedExamples.situation: A cleaner runs low on a spray product and is tempted to top up the bottle from an unlabelled drum on the shelf.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Is the refill acceptable, and what should happen instead?
workedExamples.reasoning: No. An unlabelled drum cannot be matched to an SDS, so the refill is not acceptable. Use the approved, labelled bulk container, or request the correct product from the site or the supervisor. If the drum has no label, leave it, record it and refer it to the site.

equipmentAndPpe: Labelled waste containers for each stream, as provided by the site.
Gloves and eye protection as set by the SDS and the task risk assessment.
Absorbent material and spill tools as supplied by the site.
Access to the site's hazardous chemicals register and the SDS for each product.
Waste stream record and referral form.

commonErrors.prevention: Keep streams apart in the labelled containers, and check the label before use.

commonErrors.error: Refilling a bottle from an unlabelled container.
commonErrors.prevention: Use only approved, labelled bulk containers, and refer any unlabelled drum to the site.

commonErrors.error: Disposing of an unknown material yourself.
commonErrors.prevention: Leave it in place, record it and refer it to the site.

commonErrors.error: Washing a leak toward a floor or stormwater drain.
commonErrors.prevention: Stop, contain with the site's absorbent, check the SDS and refer the clean-up.

commonErrors.error: Recording an item as disposed when it was only referred.
commonErrors.prevention: Record the action actually taken, and the person who took over the item.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: General environmental duty (Victoria): a business must reduce or eliminate the risk of harm from its waste, so far as reasonably practicable. The EPA states the duty applies to businesses and households, and that businesses which fail to meet it face significant penalties (EPA Victoria, updated 4 August 2026).

Regulated waste: the classification, storage, transport and disposal rules for regulated or industrial waste apply under environment law. This lesson does not authorise the cleaner to classify, store, transport or dispose of any regulated waste.

Hazardous chemicals and SDS: the Safe Work Australia guidance says the hazardous chemicals register must list the current SDS for each listed chemical, be kept up to date, and be readily accessible to workers.

qualityStandard: Streams separated correctly in the simulated site, with each container's label checked.
Unlabelled sealed container left in place, recorded and referred in the case study, and not binned.
Simulated leak stopped, contained with site absorbent, and referred, with no wash into a drain.
No unlabelled refill accepted, and the approved container used instead.
documentationEvidence: Waste stream record for the shift, showing what was separated and where.
Referral record for each unclear item, with location, time, description and the person notified.
Spill or leak note with the product name, the SDS reference, the action taken and the referral.
summary: Keep waste streams apart, and check the label before use.
Reduce waste through reuse and approved, labelled bulk refills only.
Leave unclear or regulated waste in place and refer it to the site.
Stop a leak, keep it out of drains, and record what was actually done.

knowledgeChecks.question: A sealed container with no label is in the recycling bin. What is correct?
options: Bin it in general waste, since it looks non-recyclable
Recycle it, since most containers can go in the yellow bin
Leave it in place, record it and refer it to the site

knowledgeChecks.question: Why keep waste streams apart?
options: It is for tidiness only, so the bins look neat on the day
Mixing spoils recycling and can create a regulated waste problem
It is not needed if the bins are emptied together by the same crew

knowledgeChecks.question: How should consumables be reduced?
options: By pouring old stock back into the containers without relabelling them
By using more paper and single-use wipes for every refill of the dispensers
By avoiding excess orders and using approved, labelled bulk refills
